goal: Run the first end-to-end content workflow on the existing DB-01 lesson and produce a reviewed draft with traceable evidence.

in_scope: Work only on Database lesson DB-01: Data Modeling and Relational Foundations.
Produce a claim-level source evidence report for the material technical claims in DB-01.
Produce a curriculum map for DB-01 covering prerequisites, scope, measurable outcomes, and outcome-to-assessment alignment.
Create a revised DB-01 draft and separate technical, pedagogical, and provenance review reports.
After reviews, update the canonical DB-01 lesson and save the run artifacts under modules/database/workflow/runs/SD-DB01-WORKFLOW-PILOT/.
Record structural and repository test results in a validation report; keep the lesson status as draft.
out_of_scope: Editing any lesson other than DB-01, the remaining case study, or another module.
Publishing learner-facing content, merging a pull request, or marking the lesson approved.
Creating vendor-specific executable labs or making production performance claims.

constraints: Write in Vietnamese while retaining standard English technical terms; target backend engineers with basic SQL and application development experience.
Use the System Design Primer as a topic map and licensed source, not as the sole technical authority or text to translate paragraph by paragraph.
For material and version-sensitive claims, record exact source URL, section, product/version where applicable, and date checked; flag unresolved claims rather than guessing.
Use original explanations, examples, diagrams, exercises, questions, and answer explanations; separately identify any adapted expression or asset.
Keep all generated lesson content at status: draft. Human approval, merge, and publication remain outside this task.
Use distinct output paths for authoring and each independent review. Stop for human judgment if a critical disagreement remains after at most two revision cycles.

definition_of_done.text: The evidence report maps each material DB-01 technical claim to a direct source and section, states applicable product/version and check date, and flags evidence gaps.

The curriculum map states DB-01 scope and non-goals, target learner and prerequisite assumptions, measurable outcomes, estimated effort, and an explicit mapping from every outcome to at least one assessment.

The draft contains the required lesson sections, a worked example, trade-offs and failure modes, a practical exercise with solution or rubric, and 5–8 knowledge checks with answer explanations and direct references.
Technical, pedagogical, and provenance reviews are recorded in separate reports with severity, evidence, and actionable findings.
The final run artifact and canonical DB-01 lesson incorporate resolved review findings, retain status: draft, and identify any remaining human decisions.
The validation report records the exact validation commands and outcomes and distinguishes structural checks from factual, legal, and pedagogical approval.
All declared outputs are committed, task state is automation_complete, and no approval or publication state is inferred.

acceptance_criteria.text: Only DB-01 and task-specific workflow run artifacts are changed; unrelated lessons and modules remain untouched.
Evidence entries identify the claim, exact URL and section, publisher, applicable version/scope, date checked, and verification status; unsupported claims are marked unresolved.
Every DB-01 learning outcome maps to at least one question or exercise, and assessment prompts are answerable from taught material.
Each reviewer reports independently to its own declared output path and does not overwrite the author draft or another review report.
Both the final run artifact and canonical DB-01 lesson declare status: draft; no unsupported claim is presented as verified.
The repository content validator, unit test suite, and task-state validator are run and their results are accurately recorded, including any host-dependent skipped test.
